import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive customer segmentation insights
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# Calculate total spending
df['TotalSpending'] = (df['MntWines'] + df['MntFruits'] + df['MntMeatProducts'] + 
                       df['MntFishProducts'] + df['MntSweetProducts'] + df['MntGoldProds'])

# Calculate age
df['Age'] = 2024 - df['Year_Birth']

# Calculate total children
df['TotalChildren'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']

# 1. Income vs Total Spending by Education (main plot)
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :2])
education_order = df.groupby('Education')['Income'].median().sort_values().index
for edu in education_order:
    mask = df['Education'] == edu
    ax1.scatter(df[mask]['Income'], df[mask]['TotalSpending'], alpha=0.5, label=edu, s=30)
ax1.set_xlabel('Income ($)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_ylabel('Total Spending ($)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_title('Customer Income vs Total Spending by Education Level', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax1.legend(title='Education', fontsize=8, title_fontsize=9)
ax1.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 2. Age Distribution
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
ax2.hist(df['Age'], bins=30, color='steelblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax2.set_xlabel('Age', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_title('Age Distribution', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 3. Spending by Category
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
spending_categories = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 
                       'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
category_totals = [df[cat].sum() for cat in spending_categories]
category_labels = ['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweets', 'Gold']
colors = plt.cm.Set3(range(len(category_labels)))
ax3.pie(category_totals, labels=category_labels, autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90, colors=colors)
ax3.set_title('Spending Distribution by Category', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# 4. Marital Status Distribution
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
ax4.barh(marital_counts.index, marital_counts.values, color='coral', edgecolor='black')
ax4.set_xlabel('Count', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_title('Marital Status Distribution', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)

# 5. Number of Children vs Spending
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
children_spending = df.groupby('TotalChildren')['TotalSpending'].mean()
ax5.bar(children_spending.index, children_spending.values, color='mediumseagreen', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.8)
ax5.set_xlabel('Number of Children', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_ylabel('Avg Total Spending ($)', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_title('Avg Spending by Children Count', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax5.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 6. Purchase Channel Preferences
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
channels = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases', 'NumDealsPurchases']
channel_totals = [df[ch].sum() for ch in channels]
channel_labels = ['Web', 'Catalog', 'Store', 'Deals']
ax6.bar(channel_labels, channel_totals, color=['#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#2ca02c', '#d62728'], 
        edgecolor='black', alpha=0.8)
ax6.set_ylabel('Total Purchases', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_title('Purchase Channel Preferences', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax6.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 7. Campaign Acceptance Rates
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
campaigns = ['AcceptedCmp1', 'AcceptedCmp2', 'AcceptedCmp3', 'AcceptedCmp4', 'AcceptedCmp5', 'Response']
acceptance_rates = [(df[cmp].sum() / len(df)) * 100 for cmp in campaigns]
campaign_labels = ['Cmp1', 'Cmp2', 'Cmp3', 'Cmp4', 'Cmp5', 'Last Cmp']
ax7.bar(campaign_labels, acceptance_rates, color='purple', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax7.set_ylabel('Acceptance Rate (%)', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
ax7.set_title('Campaign Acceptance Rates', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax7.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 8. Income Distribution by Education
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
education_income = [df[df['Education'] == edu]['Income'].dropna() for edu in education_order]
bp = ax8.boxplot(education_income, labels=education_order, patch_artist=True)
for patch in bp['boxes']:
    patch.set_facecolor('lightblue')
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax8.set_xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')
ax8.set_ylabel('Income ($)', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
ax8.set_title('Income by Education', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax8.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45, labelsize=8)
ax8.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

plt.suptitle('Customer Segmentation Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
